# Running Multiple Kernels on One Bare-Metal Server {.unnumbered}

Modern bare-metal servers offer extraordinary core counts, multi-terabyte memory configurations, and high-bandwidth PCIe fabrics. However, the standard monolithic Linux architecture operates under the assumption that a single kernel image owns and arbitrates all physical machine resources. In high-performance, real-time, isolated multi-tenant, and fault-tolerant production environments, running multiple independent kernel instances on one physical machine provides unprecedented isolation and predictability without the overhead of enterprise hypervisor virtualization layers.

This section covers the architecture, mechanics, isolation primitives, performance characteristics, and production operations required to partition bare-metal hardware and run multiple operating system kernels concurrently and transitions safely.

## Curriculum Architecture

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                     PHYSICAL BARE-METAL SERVER                          │
│                                                                         │
│   NUMA Node 0 (Host / Control Instance)      NUMA Node 1 (Guest Kernel) │
│   ┌──────────────────────────────┐          ┌─────────────────────────┐ │
│   │ Cores 0-15 (Housekeeping)    │          │ Cores 16-31 (Isolated)  │ │
│   │ 64 GB Local Memory           │          │ 64 GB Static Hugepages  │ │
│   │ Host Drivers (Root)          │          │ vfio-pci Bound Devices  │ │
│   └──────────────┬───────────────┘          └────────────┬────────────┘ │
│                  │                                       │              │
│                  ▼                                       ▼              │
│   ┌──────────────────────────────┐          ┌─────────────────────────┐ │
│   │ Primary Host Kernel (v6.x)   │          │ Dedicated Worker Kernel │ │
│   │ - OS: Ubuntu 26.04 Server    │          │ - Custom Tuned Kernel   │ │
│   │ - Management Stack (libvirt) │          │ - Direct Hardware Access│ │
│   │ - Uplink NIC (PF)            │          │ - SR-IOV Virtual Func   │ │
│   │ - Storage Controller (NVMe)  │          │ - Direct NVMe Namespace │ │
│   └──────────────┬───────────────┘          └────────────┬────────────┘ │
│                  │                                       │              │
│                  └──────────── Inter-Kernel Link ────────┘              │
│                               (ivshmem / vsock)                         │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```
